scope_note: Full-source first pass for all packet targets and contexts. Broad-date public notices retain their open XML lower bounds and publication-based historical limits; earlier accepted or same-author relations are not recounted as new links.

record_reviews.source_kind: Darwin-authored Gardeners’ Chronicle letter; broad date probe
record_reviews.summary: Darwin gives the second, much larger season of his bean-fertilisation work: netted versus open rows, 35 versus 292 pods, later 97 versus 292, and the common-bean comparison where covered pods were frequently empty. He then discusses clover, Lathyrus, New Zealand observations from Mr Swale, grasshoppers releasing stamens, and the difficulty of crossing. The final half reports Coe’s Negro Bean mixtures through successive generations, weighs crossing against simple variation, and speculates about pollen failure after self-fertilisation before asking readers for analogous cases.
record_reviews.date_assessment: XML lower bound is the open 1809 artifact and upper bound 1858-11-12; the editorial heading is [before 13 November 1858] and publication is 13 November. The long dated experiments refer to 1857 and 1858 but do not make the manuscript a conventional exact-day letter.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin authored all 16 retained body blocks. Swale, Coe, Wiegmann, Gärtner, Pallas and Berkeley are reported authorities or correspondents; their words and experimental results remain attributed rather than recast as Darwin observation. No figures or scholarly sibling sections are preserved.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin thanks Gould for procuring an authoritative answer from Dr Brewer about the cuckoo’s habits and says Yarrell’s authority was wrong. He regrets missing Gould in England, comments on Gould’s limited leisure, and invites an account of Japanese shells for geographical work. The body is a four-paragraph acknowledgement and future request, not a preserved scientific answer from Gould.
record_reviews.date_assessment: XML sent date is 1858-04-06. The receipt or composition date of Gould’s underlying enquiry/answer is not given; Darwin only says Gould procured an answer and he received it.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin is the author. Brewer and Yarrell are named authorities, and Gould’s Japanese-shell work is prospective; neither third-party material is a surviving incoming body.

evidence.quote: I write one line to return you my very sincere thanks for the kind manner in which you have so effectually & completely procured me an answer

record_reviews.summary: Darwin acknowledges Gould’s 9 April note and Cuming’s box of Californian cirripedia received the previous day. He reports publication of Fossil Lepadidae, imminent work on recent pedunculated cirripedes and progress through sessile species, promising to keep and eventually return the specimens named in one parcel.
record_reviews.date_assessment: XML date is 1851-06-02. The 9 April Gould note and specimen dispatch are received before composition, but their dates and bodies are not preserved here.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s voice is complete; Gould’s note is only referenced. Footnotes identify specimens and Cuming without turning them into incoming text.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: No matching incoming Gould note survives in this packet; this is prior context for the specimen relationship, not a new 1858-59 link.

evidence.quote: I received yesterday your note of the 9th. of April, & the small box of Californian cirripedia

record_reviews.summary: Darwin explains that he sent Agassiz a Fossil Lepadidae copy in a packet, while withholding Gould’s presentation copy because Gould belongs to the Ray Society and should receive the later Pedunculated Cirripedes volume. He reports work on sessile species and the unusual sexual anatomy of Gould’s Burmese Ibla specimens, then explicitly says the note requires no answer.
record_reviews.date_assessment: XML date is 1852-02-29. The packet and future Ray Society distribution are logistics; no incoming Gould receipt or answer is dated.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin authored the body; Agassiz and Gould’s specimen contribution are reported. The footnotes’ manuscript copy lists remain editorial evidence.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The source explicitly says it requires no answer, so it cannot be treated as a reply pair; no Gould prompt is preserved.

evidence.quote: This note, obviously requires no answer: I send it, merely in fear that you should think that I had overlooked your kindness.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin says his cirripede work is finished and that he has packed Gould’s loaned specimens. He explains the Ray Society copy decision, arranges carriage through Mrs Williams and Norgate, returns Agassiz’s specimens in the same box, reports one stolen Tetraclita variant, and recalls dissecting the Tavoy Ibla specimen.
record_reviews.date_assessment: XML date is 1854-09-09. The planned box dispatch is next week, distinct from writing and Gould’s later receipt; no incoming Gould source is supplied.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin authored all five body blocks. Gould, Agassiz, Mrs Williams and Norgate are named in logistical or reported roles; the missing former occasion is not reconstructed.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: No prompt or response endpoint is preserved. The specimen return is a custody event, not a correspondence pair.

evidence.quote: They are, I believe, all returned safely, excepting one very curious var.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin reports that Lyell says Gould has seen the last Cirripedia volume and liked it. He asks whether Gould remains a Ray Society subscriber, offers one of two retained copies if not, and explains that delayed distribution would otherwise account for Gould receiving it through the Society. He apologises for troubling him.
record_reviews.date_assessment: XML date is 1855-07-21. Lyell’s note is received a few days earlier, but Gould’s reading date and any reply are unknown.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin authored the four blocks; Lyell’s reported statement is third-party voice. The offered copy and subscription status are prospective logistics.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: No incoming Gould response is preserved. This is a membership/copy question, not a source for 2448’s cuckoo answer.

evidence.quote: In a note received a few days since from Sir C. Lyell he tells me that you have seen my last volume on Cirripedia

record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks Gardeners’ Chronicle readers how dun or mouse-coloured striped ponies are bred, whether one or both parents must be dun, and whether shoulder/leg stripes are clearer in colts. The retained source is a three-block public notice; the editorial note identifies it as the original of the 13 June 1857 published notice and points to related Eyton/Hooker material.
record_reviews.date_assessment: XML range is open lower bound 1809 to 1857-06-12, displayed [before 13 June 1857]. The lower bound is metadata machinery, not a plausible historical composition date; the publication cross-reference supplies the useful upper context.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin authored the notice; ‘readers’ are an anonymous intended audience. No reader answer survives in this source.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: It is an earlier Darwin question and same subject as Egan 2354, but not an incoming prompt for 2359; no response is preserved.

evidence.quote: Will any reader of the Gardeners’ Chronicle be so kind as to take the trouble to inform me how Dun or Mouse-coloured Ponys

record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks readers about reducing the weight of a 12-gallon deep-well bucket. He supplies the 325-foot depth, 40-pound bucket, 232-pound chain and 96-pound water figures, describes Newall’s wire rope, and asks whether zinc, gutta percha or leather could replace oak. The original is missing; the HTML is the published text.
record_reviews.date_assessment: XML range is open lower bound 1809 to 1857-07-24, displayed [before 25 July 1857]. The editorial publication date and missing original are stronger evidence than the artificial lower bound.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s two-block public notice is the surviving published text; no reader’s reply or covering letter is present.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: No incoming endpoint is preserved, and the well mechanics have no relationship to the Gould/cirripede or bean sources in this packet.

evidence.quote: I have a well 325 feet deep, and the 12-gallon bucket actually weighs 40 lbs.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks what Swayne meant by artificial fertilisation of early beans, then gives a detailed account of kidney-bean flower structure, bee position, pollen movement and three small enclosure experiments. He records failures in undisturbed flowers, qualifies the experiment’s replication, and adds observations of humble-bees cutting calyx holes and hive-bees following them. The body ends with the artificial-fertilisation question and a concern about varieties crossing.
record_reviews.date_assessment: XML date is 1857-10-18. Darwin’s dated observation and publication notice are contemporary to the source, while the earlier Swayne reference is historical bibliography; no incoming reader answer is included.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin authored the full long block. Swayne’s 1824 publication and the bees’ observed behaviour are respectively reported source and Darwin observation; the bracketed Early Mazagan sentence is editorial insertion in the body’s publication history.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: 2359 continues the same public bean investigation in 1858, but both are Darwin-authored notices and 2359 does not answer an incoming source. No direct link proposed.

evidence.quote: Not one of the undisturbed flowers set a pod, whereas the greater number (but not all) of those which I moved

record_reviews.summary: Darwin questions the writer of a Gardeners’ Chronicle weeds article about foreign seed of an indigenous species, comparing fecundity with vigour. He cites Gray’s naturalised plants and Hooker’s Sonchus, asks whether imported black mustard displaced charlock without renewed seed, and requests other cases of one weed beating another. The printed body is one long block; a later Buckman response is mentioned in the apparatus but not preserved here.
record_reviews.date_assessment: XML range is open lower bound 1809 to 1857-11-11, displayed [before 12 November 1857]. The dated newspaper article and Moor Park context constrain it to 1857; the lower XML bound is not historical evidence.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin authored the enquiry. Gray and Hooker are cited authorities, and the Gardeners’ Chronicle article writer is addressed but unnamed; Buckman’s later response is editorially reported, not present body text.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: No incoming article-writer response is preserved, and this weeds enquiry cannot be used as a prompt for the bean continuation in 2359.

evidence.quote: I have no doubt that so acute an observer has some good reason for his belief.
